schema_note: Each case has name, family, direction, root, expected_stack, strict_bytes, and notes. Planned cases may not have fixture bytes yet.

cases.name: arp-request-reply-roundtrip
cases.notes: Standard Ethernet/IPv4 ARP request and reply byte preservation: hardware_type 1, protocol_type IPv4, HLN 6, PLN 4, and the 6-octet MAC / 4-octet IPv4 sender and target addresses must round-trip unchanged (RFC 826 base header; target/arp-rfc/scope.md). Guards the existing ethernet_arp golden bytes; fixture bytes wired by later materialization steps.

cases.name: arp-unknown-opcode-raw
cases.notes: Structurally valid ARP with an unknown numeric operation value (for example RFC 5494 experimental OP_EXP1 24 / OP_EXP2 25 or an unassigned numeric opcode) must decode as ARP, preserve the raw u16 operation, and never be remapped to request/reply (arp-parameters-1; RFC 5494; target/arp-rfc/scope.md). Fixture bytes wired by later materialization steps.

cases.name: arp-variable-address-lengths
cases.notes: Nonstandard hardware_length / protocol_length ARP (for example HLN 8 and PLN 16, plus zero-length HLN/PLN) must split sender and target address byte vectors by HLN/PLN, preserve the bytes accurately, and not overflow (RFC 826 generic format; arp.yaml address_fields byte_vectors; target/arp-rfc/scope.md). Uses documentation address space only. Fixture bytes wired by later materialization steps.

cases.name: arp-gratuitous-probe
cases.notes: RFC 5227 gratuitous announcement and probe ARP are expressed through base REQUEST/REPLY with specific sender/target field conventions (zero sender or target protocol address; no new opcode), not a new ARP variant (RFC 5227 updates RFC 826; target/arp-rfc/scope.md assumption 2). Fixture bytes wired by later materialization steps.

cases.name: arp-trailing-raw-payload
cases.notes: Extra bytes after a complete ARP body remain observable as raw payload after the ARP layer (spec: trailing bytes preserved as Raw; RFC 826 fixed body length is HLN/PLN-derived). Fixture bytes wired by later materialization steps.

cases.name: arp-family-rarp-inarp-codepoints
cases.notes: ARP-family operation codepoints in scope as codepoint-only round-trippable values with no extension message bodies: RARP 3/4 (RFC 903), DRARP 5/6/7 (RFC 1931), InARP 8/9 (RFC 2390), ARP-NAK 10 (RFC 1577), MAPOS-UNARP 23 (RFC 2176). They ride the unmodified RFC 826 wire format (arp-parameters-1; target/arp-rfc/scope.md). MARS opcodes 11-22 and other unassigned values are deferred to data-only recognition (no named ergonomics). Fixture bytes wired by later materialization steps.

cases.name: ndp-router-solicitation
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.1 Router Solicitation (type 133, code 0) sent from a link-local source (fe80::/10) to the all-routers multicast ff02::2, carrying a Source Link-Layer Address option (section 4.6.1) with a documentation MAC. The 32-bit Reserved rest-of-header is sent zero. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RS/ICMPv6NDOptSrcLLAddr; libcrafter decodes the typed RouterSolicitation body and its NDP option list. The fixed 8-octet header plus the 8-octet SLLA option give strict byte agreement in both directions.

cases.name: ndp-router-advertisement
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.2 Router Advertisement (type 134, code 0) from a link-local router (fe80::/10) to the all-nodes multicast ff02::1. The rest-of-header carries Cur Hop Limit 64, the M (Managed) flag set with O clear and the six Reserved flag bits zero, and Router Lifetime 1800 s; the body carries Reachable Time and Retrans Timer words and two options in order: Prefix Information (section 4.6.2, prefix 2001:db8:1::/64 with the L and A flags set, valid/preferred lifetimes) and MTU (section 4.6.4, 1500). Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptPrefixInfo/ICMPv6NDOptMTU; libcrafter decodes the typed RouterAdvertisement body, the M/O flags from the header, and the ordered NDP option list. Both option types are fixed-width (PI 4 units, MTU 1 unit) so strict bytes hold in both directions. Scapy normalization quirk: scapy's ICMPv6ND_RA defaults the RFC 4191 Default Router Preference (Prf) field, which occupies two of RFC 4861's send-as-zero Reserved flag bits, to a non-zero value (prf=1 -> flags byte 0x08); the reference RA must be materialized with prf=0 so its flags byte (0x80, M only) matches libcrafter, which sends those Reserved bits zero per RFC 4861 section 4.2. With prf=0 the two stacks agree byte-for-byte (verified: IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes 860003484080...05dc on both sides). An agent that wants the RFC 4191 preference sets the header rest-of-header explicitly via Icmpv6::rest_of_header (honored override).

cases.name: ndp-neighbor-solicitation
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.3 Neighbor Solicitation (type 135, code 0) resolving a documentation Target Address (2001:db8:1::10), sent from a link-local source (fe80::/10) to the solicited-node multicast ff02::1:ff00:10, carrying a Source Link-Layer Address option (section 4.6.1). The 32-bit Reserved rest-of-header is sent zero and the 128-bit Target Address leads the body. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6ND_NS/ICMPv6NDOptSrcLLAddr; libcrafter decodes the typed NeighborSolicitation body (target + options). Strict bytes in both directions. A DAD-form solicitation (source ::, no SLLA) is exercised by the Rust integration test crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs.

cases.name: ndp-neighbor-advertisement
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.4 Neighbor Advertisement (type 136, code 0) for a documentation Target Address (2001:db8:1::10) sent to a link-local host (fe80::/10), carrying a Target Link-Layer Address option (section 4.6.1). The rest-of-header flags word sets S (Solicited) and O (Override) with R (Router) clear and the 29 Reserved bits zero; the 128-bit Target Address leads the body. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6ND_NA/ICMPv6NDOptDstLLAddr; libcrafter decodes the typed NeighborAdvertisement body, reporting each R/S/O flag independently. Strict bytes in both directions.

cases.name: ndp-redirect
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.5 Redirect (type 137, code 0) from a link-local router (fe80::/10) to a link-local host, advertising a better-first-hop Target Address and a Destination Address being redirected (both 128-bit fields lead the body), carrying a Target Link-Layer Address option (section 4.6.1) and a Redirected Header option (section 4.6.3) with an embedded sample packet, zero-padded to the 8-octet boundary. The 32-bit Reserved rest-of-header is sent zero. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6ND_Redirect/ICMPv6NDOptDstLLAddr/ICMPv6NDOptRedirectedHdr; libcrafter decodes the typed Redirect body (target + destination + options). Strict bytes in both directions.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-router-solicitation
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::router_solicitation_with_source_link_layer (RFC 4861 section 4.1) over IPv6 from a link-local source to ff02::2 decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RS/ICMPv6NDOptSrcLLAddr with the same Reserved word and Source Link-Layer Address, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-router-solicitation case.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-router-advertisement
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::router_advertisement_with carrying Prefix Information (RFC 4861 section 4.6.2) and MTU (section 4.6.4) options decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptPrefixInfo/ICMPv6NDOptMTU with the same Cur Hop Limit, M/O flags, Router Lifetime, Reachable Time, Retrans Timer, prefix/lifetimes, and MTU, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-router-advertisement case and proves the option-ordering round-trip. Same RFC 4191 Prf normalization quirk as ndp-router-advertisement: libcrafter sends the RFC 4861 send-as-zero Reserved flag bits (which include the RFC 4191 Prf field) as zero, so the scapy reference must use prf=0 for a strict-byte comparison; the agreed IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes are 860003484080...05dc.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-neighbor-solicitation
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::neighbor_solicitation_with_source_link_layer (RFC 4861 section 4.3) resolving 2001:db8:1::10 toward the solicited-node multicast decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_NS/ICMPv6NDOptSrcLLAddr with the same Reserved word, Target Address, and Source Link-Layer Address, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-neighbor-solicitation case.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-neighbor-advertisement
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::neighbor_advertisement_with_target_link_layer (RFC 4861 section 4.4) with S and O set and R clear decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_NA/ICMPv6NDOptDstLLAddr with the same R/S/O flags word, Target Address, and Target Link-Layer Address, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-neighbor-advertisement case.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-redirect
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::redirect (RFC 4861 section 4.5) carrying a Target Link-Layer Address (section 4.6.1) and a Redirected Header option (section 4.6.3) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_Redirect/ICMPv6NDOptDstLLAddr/ICMPv6NDOptRedirectedHdr with the same Reserved word, Target and Destination Addresses, link-layer address, and embedded redirected packet (zero-padded to the 8-octet boundary), byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-redirect case.

cases.name: ndp-ra-route-rdnss-dnssl-mtu
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.2 Router Advertisement (type 134, code 0) from a link-local router (fe80::/10) to the all-nodes multicast ff02::1, carrying the four standards-track NDP option extensions in order: Route Information (RFC 4191 section 2.3, prefix 2001:db8:2::/48 with Prf High and a 1800 s route lifetime), RDNSS (RFC 8106 section 5.1, server 2001:db8:ffff::1, lifetime 900 s), DNSSL (RFC 8106 section 5.2, search list example.com., lifetime 900 s), and MTU (RFC 4861 section 4.6.4, 1500). Cur Hop Limit 64, M/O clear, the six Reserved flag bits zero, Router Lifetime 1800 s, Reachable Time and Retrans Timer zero. Byte agreement proved by materializing the same stack in Scapy (ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptRouteInfo/ICMPv6NDOptRDNSS/ICMPv6NDOptDNSSL/ICMPv6NDOptMTU, prf=0 per the ndp-router-advertisement note) and libcrafter and diffing the IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes: identical (8600c1f4...05dc). One representational note: scapy's ICMPv6NDOptRouteInfo always emits the full 16 prefix octets (RFC 4191 Length 3), so the byte-proof pins libcrafter's Route Information to the same 16-octet form via Icmpv6 NdpOption::route_information_raw(prefix_octets=16); the crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs round-trip uses the natural length-derived form, where a /48 prefix carries 8 octets (Length 2) — both are RFC 4191 section 2.3 valid. The primary round-trip correctness gate is crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::router_advertisement_round_trips_with_route_rdnss_dnssl_mtu.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-ra-route-rdnss-dnssl-mtu
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::router_advertisement_with carrying Route Information (RFC 4191), RDNSS and DNSSL (RFC 8106), and MTU (RFC 4861) options decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptRouteInfo/ICMPv6NDOptRDNSS/ICMPv6NDOptDNSSL/ICMPv6NDOptMTU with the same flags, lifetimes, route preference and prefix, DNS server, search-list domain, and MTU, byte-for-byte, and the four-option order preserved. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-ra-route-rdnss-dnssl-mtu case (Route Information pinned to the 16-octet/Length-3 form to match scapy's encoder; verified IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes 8600c1f4...05dc).

cases.name: ndp-pref64
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.2 Router Advertisement carrying a single PREF64 option (RFC 8781 section 4) that advertises the RFC 6052 Well-Known NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96 with a Scaled Lifetime of 75 (units of 8 seconds) and PLC 0 (96-bit prefix). The option is exactly two 8-octet units (no padding). Byte agreement proved by materializing ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptPREF64(scaledlifetime=75, plc=0, prefix=64:ff9b::) in Scapy and libcrafter NdpOption::pref64(75, 96, 64:ff9b::) and diffing the IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes: identical (86005abb...0064ff9b...). The primary round-trip correctness gate is crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::router_advertisement_round_trips_with_pref64.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-pref64
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::router_advertisement_with carrying a PREF64 option (RFC 8781) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptPREF64 with the same Scaled Lifetime, PLC, and high-96 NAT64 prefix, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-pref64 case.

cases.name: ndp-captive-portal
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.2 Router Advertisement carrying a single Captive Portal option (RFC 8910 section 2.3) whose URI is https://example.com/portal, NUL-padded to the 8-octet boundary (RFC 8910 section 2.3: the option is padded with NUL to a multiple of 8 bytes). Byte agreement proved by materializing ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptCaptivePortal(URI=https://example.com/portal) in Scapy and libcrafter NdpOption::captive_portal("https://example.com/portal") and diffing the IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes: identical (86002d43...68747470733a2f2f6578616d706c652e636f6d2f706f7274616c00000000). The primary round-trip correctness gate is crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::neighbor_solicitation_round_trips_with_captive_portal (the Rust case carries the same option on a Neighbor Solicitation to exercise it on a non-RA message).

cases.name: crafter-ndp-captive-portal
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::router_advertisement_with carrying a Captive Portal option (RFC 8910) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptCaptivePortal with the same URI (trailing NUL padding stripped on decode), byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-captive-portal case.

cases.name: ndp-unknown-option
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 4861 section 4.2 Router Advertisement carrying one synthetic unknown NDP option (type 253, the RFC 4727 experimental option codepoint) with Length 1 (one 8-octet unit) and six value bytes deadbeefcafe. Per RFC 4861 section 4.6 and spec.md, an unknown option type is preserved as raw option bytes rather than rejected or remapped; libcrafter decodes it as NdpOption::Unknown and re-encodes it verbatim. Byte agreement proved by materializing ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptUnknown(type=253, len=1, data=deadbeefcafe) in Scapy and libcrafter NdpOption::unknown(253, deadbeefcafe) and diffing the IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes: identical (86001d7f...fd01deadbeefcafe). The primary round-trip correctness gate is crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::router_advertisement_round_trips_with_unknown_option.

cases.name: crafter-ndp-unknown-option
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::router_advertisement_with carrying a synthetic unknown NDP option (type 253) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6ND_RA/ICMPv6NDOptUnknown with the same option type, length, and value bytes, byte-for-byte, proving unknown-option preservation through re-encode. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter ndp-unknown-option case. Scapy lacks a native class for two of this effort's standards-track options — the Nonce option (RFC 3971, no ICMPv6NDOptNonce in scapy 2.5+) and the RA Flags Extension option (RFC 5175, no ICMPv6NDOptRAFlagsExt) — so those two options have no native-class byte-proof case; they are covered by the crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs round-trips and the unit tests in crafter/src/protocols/icmp/v6/message/ndp_option.rs, and on the wire they materialize as ICMPv6NDOptUnknown (type 14 / type 26) exactly like this case. This documented limitation is recorded here rather than failing the suite.

cases.name: mldv1-general-query
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 2710 section 3 MLDv1 General Query (type 130, code 0) from a link-local source (fe80::/10) to the all-nodes multicast ff02::1, hop limit 1. The Multicast Address is the unspecified address (::) and the rest-of-header carries Maximum Response Delay 10000 ms and a zero Reserved field. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6MLQuery(mladdr='::', mrd=10000); libcrafter Icmpv6::mld_general_query(10000) decodes the typed MulticastListenerMessage body and the header-derived max_response_delay. Byte agreement proved by materializing the same stack in scapy 2.7 and libcrafter and diffing the IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes: identical (820059082710000000000000000000000000000000000000). The primary round-trip correctness gate is crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::mldv1_general_query_round_trips.

cases.name: crafter-mldv1-general-query
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::mld_general_query (RFC 2710 section 3) over IPv6 from a link-local source to ff02::1 decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6MLQuery with the same unspecified Multicast Address and Maximum Response Delay, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter mldv1-general-query case (verified IPv6-level ICMPv6 bytes 820059082710...).

cases.name: mldv1-report
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 2710 section 3 MLDv1 Multicast Listener Report (type 131, code 0) announcing that the link-local source listens to the documentation-scope group ff1e::db8:1, hop limit 1. The Maximum Response Delay is meaningful only on a Query, so it is sent zero (RFC 2710 section 3.3). Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6MLReport(mladdr='ff1e::db8:1'); libcrafter Icmpv6::mld_report(ff1e::db8:1) decodes the typed MulticastListenerMessage body. Byte agreement proved against scapy 2.7 by materialization diff: identical (8300646c00000000ff1e000000000000000000000db80001). Primary correctness gate: crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::mldv1_report_round_trips.

cases.name: crafter-mldv1-report
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::mld_report (RFC 2710 section 3) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6MLReport with the same group Multicast Address and zero Maximum Response Delay, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter mldv1-report case.

cases.name: mldv1-done
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 2710 section 3 MLDv1 Multicast Listener Done (type 132, code 0) announcing that the link-local source is ceasing to listen to the documentation-scope group ff1e::db8:1 (the multicast analogue of an IGMP Leave), sent to the all-routers multicast ff02::2, hop limit 1. The Maximum Response Delay is zero. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6MLDone(mladdr='ff1e::db8:1'); libcrafter Icmpv6::mld_done(ff1e::db8:1) decodes the typed MulticastListenerMessage body. Byte agreement proved against scapy 2.7 by materialization diff: identical (8400713f00000000ff1e000000000000000000000db80001). Primary correctness gate: crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::mldv1_done_round_trips.

cases.name: crafter-mldv1-done
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::mld_done (RFC 2710 section 3) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6MLDone with the same group Multicast Address and zero Maximum Response Delay, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter mldv1-done case.

cases.name: mldv2-report-two-records
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 3810 section 5.2 (IANA now cites RFC 9777) MLDv2 Version 2 Multicast Listener Report (type 143, code 0) with TWO Multicast Address Records: record 0 MODE_IS_INCLUDE (rtype 1) for group ff1e::db8:1 with two sources (2001:db8::101, 2001:db8::102) and record 1 MODE_IS_EXCLUDE (rtype 2) for group ff1e::db8:2 with no sources, sent from a link-local source to the all-MLDv2-routers multicast ff02::16, hop limit 1. The Nr of Mcast Address Records (2) and each record's Number of Sources are auto-filled. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6MLReport2(records=[ICMPv6MLDMultAddrRec(rtype=1, dst='ff1e::db8:1', sources=[...]), ICMPv6MLDMultAddrRec(rtype=2, dst='ff1e::db8:2')]); libcrafter Icmpv6::mldv2_report([...]) decodes the typed Mldv2Report body, the header-derived record count, and each MulticastAddressRecord (type, group, source list). Byte agreement proved against scapy 2.7 by materialization diff: identical (8f00f8a00000000201000002ff1e000000000000000000000db8000120010db800000000000000000000010120010db800000000000000000000010202000000ff1e000000000000000000000db80002). Exercises the spec.md edge case 'an MLDv2 report with multiple multicast address records and source lists round-trips'. Primary correctness gate: crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::mldv2_report_with_two_records_round_trips.

cases.name: crafter-mldv2-report-two-records
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::mldv2_report with two Multicast Address Records (MODE_IS_INCLUDE with two sources + MODE_IS_EXCLUDE with none, RFC 3810 section 5.2) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6MLReport2 with two ICMPv6MLDMultAddrRec records carrying the same record types, groups, and source lists, and the same auto-filled record/source counts, byte-for-byte. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter mldv2-report-two-records case.

cases.name: mldv2-general-query
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. RFC 3810 section 5.1 MLDv2 Version 2 General Query (type 130, code 0 — the longer body shape that shares type 130 with the MLDv1 Query and is disambiguated by body length) with the unspecified Multicast Address (::), Maximum Response Code 10000, QRV 2, QQIC 125, and no sources, from a link-local source to ff02::1, hop limit 1. Scapy materializes IPv6/ICMPv6MLQuery2(mladdr='::', mrd=10000, QRV=2, QQIC=125); libcrafter Icmpv6::mldv2_query(10000, Mldv2Query::new(::).querier_robustness(2).querier_query_interval_code(125)) decodes the typed Mldv2Query body (NOT mis-decoded as MLDv1). Byte agreement proved against scapy 2.7 by materialization diff: identical (820056872710000000000000000000000000000000000000027d0000). Primary correctness gate: crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::mldv2_general_query_round_trips.

cases.name: crafter-mldv2-general-query
cases.notes: libcrafter Icmpv6::mldv2_query (RFC 3810 section 5.1) decodes in Scapy as IPv6/ICMPv6MLQuery2 with the same Multicast Address, Maximum Response Code, QRV, QQIC, and (empty) source list, byte-for-byte, and is selected as the MLDv2 query (type 130 longer body) rather than the MLDv1 query. Mirrors the scapy_to_libcrafter mldv2-general-query case.

cases.name: icmpv6-extended-echo-request
cases.notes: RFC 8335 ICMPv6 Extended Echo Request (type 160, code 0): the 16-bit Identifier, 8-bit Sequence Number, and L (Local) bit ride the ICMPv6 header rest-of-header, then an RFC 4884 ICMP Extension Structure carrying a single Interface Identification Object (class 3) names the probed interface by ifIndex — the exact byte layout of the ICMPv4 Extended Echo Request (already covered by icmpv4-extended-echo-request) with type 160 and an IPv6-pseudo-header checksum. DOCUMENTED LIMITATION: scapy 2.5+/2.7 has NO native ICMPv6 class for extended echo (no ICMPv6ExtEchoRequest), so there is no native-class scapy byte-proof or strict-bytes interop case for this family — it would decode as a raw ICMPv6 type 160 payload. Its correctness is gated instead by the Rust round-trip crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::extended_echo_request_with_interface_identification_round_trips and the per-module unit tests in crafter/src/protocols/icmp/v6/message/extended_echo.rs (which assert the on-wire type/id/seq/flag byte and the embedded Interface Identification Object), mirroring how the ICMPv4 extended-echo case is byte-proven. Recorded here rather than failing the suite.

cases.name: icmpv6-extended-echo-reply
cases.notes: RFC 8335 ICMPv6 Extended Echo Reply (type 161): echoes the Identifier and Sequence Number, the Code reports the query result (0-4), and the flag byte packs the State (top 3 bits) plus the A (Active), 4 (IPv4), and 6 (IPv6) status bits; the reply carries no body. DOCUMENTED LIMITATION: as with the request (icmpv6-extended-echo-request), scapy 2.5+/2.7 has no native ICMPv6 extended-echo class, so there is no native-class byte-proof; correctness is gated by the Rust round-trip crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::extended_echo_reply_with_state_round_trips and the extended_echo.rs unit tests (which assert the State/A/4/6 flag byte and per-code round-trip). Recorded here rather than failing the suite.

cases.name: icmpv6-node-information-query
cases.notes: RFC 4620 (EXPERIMENTAL) ICMPv6 Node Information Query (type 139): the Qtype and Flags ride the ICMPv6 header rest-of-header and the body carries an 8-byte Nonce plus opaque Data (the Subject, here a 128-bit IPv6 address for a Node Addresses query, Qtype 3). Scapy 2.7 does carry native Node Information classes (ICMPv6NIQueryName/ICMPv6NIQueryIPv6/ICMPv6NIQueryNOOP and the NIReply* set), but libcrafter intentionally keeps the Node Information Data field opaque (RFC 4620 leaves the Data layout Qtype-dependent and the family is experimental), so there is no field-by-field typed-stack mapping to scapy's class hierarchy; a strict typed-stack interop case is therefore not asserted here. Correctness is gated by the Rust round-trips crafter/tests/icmpv6_ndp.rs::node_information_query_round_trips and ::node_information_response_round_trips (build -> compile -> decode_from_l3 -> assert Qtype/Flags/Nonce/Data -> byte-stable recompile) and the node_info.rs unit tests. Recorded here as a documented limitation rather than failing the suite.

cases.name: dns-soa-srv-records

cases.name: dns-raw-unknown-records
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. Authoritative response carrying an unknown private-use numeric TYPE (65280) plus the deferred NSEC3PARAM (51), TLSA (52), KEY (25), and NAPTR (35) types, each as opaque RDATA carried via DNSRR(type=N, rdata=...) on the Scapy reference; libcrafter decodes every answer to DnsRecordData::Raw and recompiles the same bytes. Strict bytes in both directions.

cases.name: dns-edns-opt-basic
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. Response carrying several EDNS(0) OPT pseudo-records in the additional section with a root owner name and empty option list, spanning the bare default, non-default UDP payload sizes (512, 1232, 65535) in the OPT CLASS, a non-zero extended RCODE, a non-default EDNS version, and the DO flag set and clear packed into the OPT TTL. Scapy DNSRROPT and libcrafter DnsRecord::opt pack the same wire fields, so strict bytes hold in both directions.

cases.name: dns-edns-options
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. Response carrying one EDNS(0) OPT pseudo-record whose RDATA holds an ordered EDNS option list: NSID (3), COOKIE (10), Padding (12), DAU (5, a mnemonic without a libcrafter constructor), and an unknown option code (65534). Each OPTION-DATA payload is raw hex carried verbatim as a generic EDNS0TLV(optcode=N, optdata=...) on the Scapy reference and as an EdnsOption on libcrafter, preserving the exact code and data bytes in a fixed order. Strict bytes in both directions.

cases.name: dnssec-ds-dnskey-rrsig
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. Authoritative response carrying one DS (Key Tag, Algorithm, Digest Type, opaque Digest), one DNSKEY (Flags, Protocol, Algorithm, opaque Public Key), and one RRSIG (Type Covered, Algorithm, Labels, Original TTL, Signature Expiration, Signature Inception, Key Tag, uncompressed Signer's Name, opaque Signature) answer per RFC 4034. The numeric fields and digest/key/signature material are wire data only with no cryptographic validation; Scapy DNSRRDS/DNSRRDNSKEY/DNSRRRSIG and libcrafter DnsRecord::ds/dnskey/rrsig pack the same wire fields and the Signer's Name is uncompressed, so strict bytes hold in both directions.

cases.name: dnssec-nsec-bitmaps
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. Authoritative response carrying two NSEC (type 47) answers whose Type Bit Maps (RFC 4034 Section 4.1.2) exercise the full encoder: the first answer is the RFC 4034 Section 4.3 example (owner alfa.example.com., next name host.example.com., present types A/MX/RRSIG/NSEC plus the unknown codepoint TYPE1234, spanning window block 0 and window block 4); the second answer feeds an unsorted list with a duplicate A entry spanning window blocks 0, 1, and 255. libcrafter DnsTypeBitmaps and the Scapy DNSRRNSEC reference (RRlist2bitmap) both sort, de-duplicate, and emit minimal window-ordered bitmaps, so the decoded type set agrees and the minimal encoding is deterministic in both directions; the byte policy is documented as normalized because libcrafter normalizes the input set on construction.

cases.name: dnssec-nsec3
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. Authoritative response carrying three NSEC3 (type 50) answers per RFC 5155 Section 3.2: answer one has a non-empty salt, a non-empty next hashed owner name, and multiple type bitmap entries (A/NS/SOA/RRSIG/DNSKEY) in a single window block; answer two has an empty salt (Salt Length 0 omits the Salt field); answer three uses an unknown hash algorithm value (0xfe) and an unknown high type bitmap codepoint (TYPE65280) spanning a later window block. The hash algorithm, flags, iterations, salt, and next hashed owner material is wire data only with no cryptographic validation, and salt and hash fields are carried and normalized as bytes rather than text. Scapy DNSRRNSEC3 and libcrafter DnsRecord::nsec3 pack the same uncompressed wire fields, so strict bytes hold in both directions.

cases.name: dns-svcb-https
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. Authoritative response carrying three SVCB/HTTPS (type 64/65) service-binding answers per RFC 9460 / RFC 9461: an SVCB AliasMode answer (SvcPriority 0, non-root target, empty SvcParams); an HTTPS ServiceMode answer (non-zero SvcPriority, root target) carrying the mandatory/alpn/no-default-alpn/port/ipv4hint/ipv6hint/dohpath params supplied out of key order; and an SVCB ServiceMode answer carrying an unknown SvcParamKey (65280) alongside a named key. Each SvcParamValue is opaque wire data carried verbatim, and both libcrafter SvcParams and the reference RDATA builder sort the params into strictly increasing SvcParamKey order. Scapy's high-level SvcParam field re-interprets known keys and rejects raw port/ipvNhint bytes, so the backend builds the exact RDATA octets and hands them to a generic DNSRR; libcrafter materializes the same bytes through DnsRecord::svcb / ::https and SvcParams, so strict bytes hold in both directions.

cases.name: dns-section-placement
cases.notes: Oracle fixture case. A single authoritative response that places one record in each DNS section per RFC 1035 Section 4.1.1: one question (QDCOUNT), one A answer (ANCOUNT, example.com. -> 192.0.2.10), one NS authority record (NSCOUNT, example.com. -> ns1.example.com.), and two additional records (ARCOUNT) - a non-OPT A glue record (ns1.example.com. -> 192.0.2.53) followed by an EDNS(0) OPT pseudo-record (RFC 6891, root owner, UDP payload size 1232, empty options). Both backends materialize the answer (an=), authority (ns=), and additional (ar=) sections from independent plan keys; the case proves placement and counts survive decode and recompile and that no record migrates between sections. Every name is uncompressed and every value is stable, so Scapy DNS(an=...,ns=...,ar=...) and libcrafter agree byte-for-byte in both directions.
